questions.q: Fertilisation typically occurs in the:
questions.exp: Sperm meets the ovum in the ampulla (lateral 1/3) of the fallopian tube within 24 hours of ovulation.
optExp: Cervix is the gateway, not site of fertilisation.
Sperm pass through, not the site.

questions.q: Implantation of the blastocyst typically occurs:
opts: In the uterine fundus on days 6–7
In the fallopian tube on day 1
questions.exp: The blastocyst implants in the uterine endometrium (usually fundus) around day 6-7 post-fertilisation.

questions.q: During week 2, the inner cell mass forms:
questions.exp: Week 2 = bilaminar disc: the inner cell mass forms epiblast (dorsal) and hypoblast (ventral).

questions.q: In week 2, the trophoblast differentiates into:
questions.exp: Trophoblast → cytotrophoblast (inner, mitotic) + syncytiotrophoblast (outer, invasive, hormone-producing).
optExp: Cavities form in week 2 but are separate.

questions.q: hCG is produced by:
questions.exp: Syncytiotrophoblast produces hCG, which maintains the corpus luteum to sustain progesterone in early pregnancy.
optExp: Cytotrophoblast is the proliferative inner layer.
Corpus luteum makes progesterone in response to hCG.

questions.q: Gastrulation occurs during which week of development?
questions.exp: Gastrulation occurs in week 3, forming the three germ layers from the epiblast via the primitive streak.

questions.q: The first visible sign of gastrulation is:
questions.exp: The primitive streak appears on the dorsal epiblast, marking the start of gastrulation and the body's craniocaudal axis.

questions.q: During gastrulation, epiblast cells that migrate through the primitive streak and DISPLACE hypoblast become:
questions.exp: First migrating epiblast cells push hypoblast aside and form endoderm; later migrants form mesoderm; remaining epiblast = ectoderm.

questions.q: Which germ layer gives rise to the nervous system?
questions.exp: Neural tube derived from ectoderm forms the CNS; neural crest cells form much of PNS.

questions.q: Which germ layer gives rise to the gut epithelium, liver, and pancreas?
questions.exp: Endoderm forms the lining of the GI tract, respiratory tract, and parenchyma of liver/pancreas.
optExp: Mesoderm forms muscle, bone, kidneys, cardiovascular.
Neural crest forms PNS, melanocytes, etc.

questions.q: The notochord:
questions.exp: The notochord is a mesodermal structure that induces overlying ectoderm to form the neural plate; persists as nucleus pulposus in adult.
optExp: Spinal cord forms from neural tube.

questions.q: The Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) pathway primarily controls:
questions.exp: SHH signalling regulates left-right asymmetry, limb patterning (digit number), ventral CNS, and many other developmental processes.
optExp: SHH is not primarily an apoptosis pathway.
SHH not directly involved in implantation.

questions.q: The Notch signalling pathway controls:
questions.exp: Notch signalling determines cell fate via direct cell-cell contact (NICD cleavage activates target genes). Mutations cause cancer or developmental defects.

questions.q: Organogenesis primarily occurs during:
questions.exp: Most organs form between weeks 4-8 (embryonic period). The fetal period (week 9-birth) is for growth and maturation.

questions.q: During the fetal period (week 9 onwards):
opts: Organs grow and mature in function
Gastrulation and germ layer formation occurs
questions.exp: Fetal period is mostly growth and functional maturation of organs that formed earlier.

questions.q: Neural tube closes around which day post-fertilisation?
questions.exp: Neural tube closure begins ~day 22 and completes by day 28. Failure → neural tube defects (spina bifida, anencephaly).

questions.q: Folate supplementation in pregnancy reduces risk of:
questions.exp: Folate supplementation prior to conception and in early pregnancy significantly reduces neural tube defects.
optExp: Some weak association but not primary.
Folate not strongly protective for cardiac.

questions.q: A morula consists of approximately:
questions.exp: After cleavage, the embryo forms a solid ball of 16-32 cells called the morula, before cavitating into a blastocyst.

questions.q: The blastocyst consists of:
questions.exp: Blastocyst = trophoblast (outer, → placenta) + inner cell mass/embryoblast (→ embryo) around a fluid-filled blastocoel.

questions.q: Somites are derived from:
questions.exp: Paraxial mesoderm segments into somites, giving rise to vertebrae (sclerotome), skeletal muscle (myotome), and dermis (dermatome).

questions.q: Surfactant production by Type II pneumocytes begins around:
questions.exp: Surfactant production starts around week 24-28 but is adequate by ~35 weeks. Premature birth → respiratory distress.

questions.q: The foramen ovale shunts blood from:
opts: Shunts blood from left atrium to right atrium
Shunts blood from right atrium to left atrium, bypassing the lungs
Shunts blood from left ventricle to right ventricle
Connects pulmonary artery to ascending aorta
Connects umbilical vein to inferior vena cava
questions.exp: In utero, the foramen ovale shunts oxygenated blood from RA to LA, bypassing non-functional lungs.

questions.q: The ductus arteriosus connects:
opts: Connects right atrium to left atrium
Connects pulmonary artery to descending aorta
Connects umbilical vein to inferior vena cava
Connects ascending aorta to superior vena cava
Connects hepatic vein to cardiac circulation
questions.exp: Ductus arteriosus shunts blood from the pulmonary trunk to the descending aorta, bypassing the fetal lungs.

questions.q: The mesoderm gives rise to all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Gut epithelium is endoderm-derived. Mesoderm gives rise to muscle, bone, cardiovascular, urogenital, dermis.

questions.q: Neural crest cells derive from and give rise to all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Liver hepatocytes are endoderm-derived. Neural crest contributes to melanocytes, PNS, adrenal medulla, parts of heart, etc.

questions.q: The teratogenic period of greatest risk is generally:
questions.exp: Most teratogens cause major malformations during weeks 3-8 (organogenesis). Before week 3 = all-or-none. After week 8 = mainly growth/functional defects.

questions.q: The syncytiotrophoblast is responsible for:
questions.exp: Syncytiotrophoblast erodes maternal tissue to embed the blastocyst and secretes hCG to maintain corpus luteum.
optExp: Inner cell mass becomes the embryo.
